Rustic Apple Cinnamon Skillet Tart

By Emily | Published Oct 14, 2026 | 142 Comments

A Love Letter to Autumn Apples

Every year when the morning air turns crisp and the leaves in upstate New York begin their amber transformation, I find myself thinking of my grandmother Clara's orchard. The scent of woodsmoke drifting over the orchard fence, the sound of boots crunching through damp grass, and the wooden bushel crates overflowing with freshly picked apples.

-- Advertisement: Sign up for the Best Wine Club --

I remember sitting on her worn wooden porch stool while she peeled apples with an antique paring knife, never breaking the peel. She would tell me that the secret to a great skillet tart isn't fancy machinery or hours of lamination—it is simply respecting the fruit and letting the oven's high heat caramelize the natural sugars.

Through college, grad school, and moving into my first tiny apartment with a stove that barely held 350 degrees, this tart was my sanctuary. I made it for roommates, for rainy Sunday reading sessions, and now for my own children who hover around the kitchen island waiting for the timer to ring.

Let's talk about apple varieties for a moment. You want an apple that holds its shape under heat without turning into applesauce. Honeycrisp, Braeburn, Pink Lady, or Jonagold all perform admirably here. Avoid Red Delicious at all costs—they turn mealy and disappoint everyone.

Recipe Details

Prep Time: 20 mins | Cook Time: 40 mins | Total: 1 hour | Servings: 6

Ingredients

  • 3 Honeycrisp apples, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp ground cinnamon
  • 2 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed
  • 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed
  • 1 large egg, beaten for wash
  • 1 pinch salt

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) and lightly grease a 10-inch cast iron skillet.
  2. Roll out puff pastry gently and fit it into the skillet, letting the edges fold naturally.
  3. Toss sliced apples in a bowl with brown sugar, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
  4. Arrange the apple slices in concentric circles inside the pastry crust and dot the top with chilled butter cubes.
  5. Brush the pastry edges with beaten egg wash and bake for 38 to 40 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling.
  6. Cool 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with vanilla bean ice cream.
